question: A 58-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his family because of severe upper back pain, which he describes as ripping. The pain started suddenly 1 hour ago while he was watching television. He has hypertension for 13 years, but he is not compliant with his medications. He denies the use of nicotine, alcohol or illicit drugs. His temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), the heart rate is 110/min and the blood pressure is 182/81 mm Hg in the right arm and 155/71 mm Hg in the left arm. CT scan of the chest shows an intimal flap limited to the descending aorta. Intravenous opioid analgesia is started. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of this patient condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with severe ripping back pain" -> "CT scan shows intimal flap in descending aorta" -> "Diagnosis of aortic dissection confirmed" -> "Management requires blood pressure control" -> "Intravenous esmolol is effective for rapid blood pressure control" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has hypertension and tachycardia" -> "Intimal flap indicates aortic dissection" -> "Immediate management is crucial to prevent complications" -> "Intravenous esmolol can quickly lower heart rate and blood pressure" -> "Esmolol is preferred in acute settings" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Severe upper back pain suggests possible aortic dissection" -> "CT scan reveals intimal flap" -> "Aortic dissection management includes blood pressure control" -> "Intravenous esmolol provides rapid control" -> "Other options are less effective in acute setting" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has sudden onset severe pain" -> "CT scan confirms aortic dissection" -> "Hypertension is present" -> "Immediate blood pressure management is necessary" -> "Intravenous esmolol is suitable for acute management" -> 88%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms consistent with an aortic dissection, characterized by severe ripping back pain and differential blood pressure readings in the arms. The CT scan confirms the presence of an intimal flap in the descending aorta. In cases of aortic dissection, especially with hypertension, the immediate goal is to lower the heart rate and blood pressure to reduce stress on the aorta. Intravenous esmolol, a beta-blocker, is the best choice for rapid control of heart rate and blood pressure in this acute setting. Emergency surgical intervention may be necessary later, but the immediate management focuses on medical stabilization.
